needs_pass2_reason: All PDF-derived tables get a blind second pass; text layer was OCR-like (garbled spacing, +/- signs mangled), so tables were typed from the page images after cross-checking the text layer numbers.
experimental_method: Steady-state gas-dissolution microcalorimeter; heat of solution of hydrocarbon gases in water at 15 and 35 C, standard-state dH0 obtained using second virial coefficients.
uncertainties_stated: Twice the standard deviation of the mean; accuracy of the method about 1 percent; up to ~2 percent systematic error possible at 35 C depending on gas-syringe temperature (controlled at 25 C to minimise).
quality_remarks: Table I propene van't Hoff (Wilhelm) uncertainty printed +-29 on 27 (likely misprint, kept as printed). Table I i-C4H10 van't Hoff 21.1 has a smudge after it in the scan; read as 21.1. Footnote letter 'a' in header of col 1 has a stray mark in the scan.
not_extracted_tables: Table III (dCp at 25 C): derived by authors by fitting dH0 vs T (Eq. 1) and literature comparison, not a direct measurement

row_counts.table_1: printed 11 gas rows (each with an uncertainty line); written 11 data rows + 11 label rows
row_counts.table_2: printed 11 gas rows; written 11 data rows + 11 label rows

extraction_notes: Gas label rows inserted before each data row (rule 10); -dH0 printed positive so mapping scale is -1. Text-layer garbles such as 'Calls' (C3H8), '21.1:' and '-+' signs were resolved from the image. Table 1 and 2 data cells matched text layer numbers. Columns c and d are literature van't Hoff values.
pass2_diff: Both tables 11 rows, all data numbers identical; only token differences are gas-name digits kept in data rows by pass 2.
